SR-006Gate/tier harness enforces required stepsre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall run the required steps of the gate that must next be passed (the strictness selector cached in docs/stage) and fail that gate when a required tool is missing, reporting SKIP(missing) rather than silently passing — and, on a claimed work branch (one whose history holds a docs/work/active/<branch>/ claim), SKIP its generated-artifact freshness steps with a stated trunk-lane reason, generated artifacts being trunk-only, while every non-freshness step still runs.

Rationale

Realizes SN-004 (gates enforce their stage's checks), SN-008 (no false pass) and the dissolved edge expectation that a missing tool fails, never skips. A sanctioned SKIP class of this harness's own step plan is not a second crossing observable, it is the same one qualified. The skip is not a weakening: a work branch cannot commit generated artifacts at all (concurrency-restructure §5.2), so demanding their freshness there would force the very conflict the rule deletes; the skip is reported, never silent, and any signal ambiguity resolves toward the full trunk checks.

SR-007Declared stack profile, refused when it is brokenre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall read the toolchain (format/lint/test commands, tiers, coverage, arch-map mode) from the declared stack profile so a stack swap edits only that declaration, failing loudly on a malformed profile or a non-integer coverage threshold rather than proceeding on a bad one.

Rationale

Realizes SN-003 — the kit is stack-agnostic; the harness is re-pointed by declaration, not by editing a kit script. Reading a declaration and REFUSING a broken one are one obligation, not two: a reader that proceeds on a malformed profile has not read it. A MISSING DECLARED BINARY is deliberately no part of it — SR-006 already states that verbatim as its own ("fail that gate when a required tool is missing"), which is why LLR-008 decomposes from both rows rather than one.

SR-017Always-on secrets flooracceptance owed

Requirement

When a session attempts to commit or push content matching a secret pattern, the system shall refuse at the hook floor — scanning every commit's staged diff, message and outgoing range regardless of the privacy toggle, and naming the finding — unless the declared secrets_scan dial is explicitly false.

Rationale

Realizes SN-009 — a credential that reaches a shared branch must be treated as disclosed and rotated, and expunging it from history is a rewrite every clone has to follow, so the cheap moment to catch it is before the commit and the expensive one is any moment after. Folding the scan into the privacy toggle was rejected: that makes the highest-severity check opt-in alongside a preference. The one opt-out is an explicit declaration, so turning it off is a visible act.

Title
The privacy scan names each leak by its location and class, and its exit code reports whether it found one
Detail
Each leak the privacy scan finds, in the staged diff, a commit message, an outgoing commit range or the sweep over the tracked files, prints on its own line naming its location (a tracked file's path and line, or the commit) and its class label, and the run then prints one summary line counting the findings and naming the scan and the layers that ran; a clean run prints one clean line naming the scan and the layers. With both layers off it scans nothing, says so and exits 0. A scan it runs exits 1 when it printed a finding and 0 when it found none.
Rationale
The hooks and the harness step read the scan's verdict from its exit code alone, and a person reads the lines to find the leak; naming the layers that ran keeps a run with a layer off from reading as a clean one.

SR-018Privacy gate two-axisacceptance owed

Requirement

When the declared privacy_check dial is on, the system shall additionally refuse, at the same hook floor, a commit or push carrying a PII/identity class — exempting configured author identities.

Rationale

Realizes SN-009 — identity and PII classes are a policy choice a repo makes about its own contributors, unlike a leaked credential, which is a defect in every repo. Making them always-on was rejected because the exemption list they need is project-specific: a repo that has not declared its author identities would have the layer firing on its own commit metadata, and the fix would be to silence the scanner rather than to configure it.

SR-019Pre-commit hook floorre-accept owed

Requirement

The pre-commit hook shall run the integrity + secrets floor on every commit, agent-neutrally — a LOCAL floor, bypassable by the session (git commit --no-verify), so it discharges "no unchecked write enters governed state" only as a PAIR with the hosted re-run of the same checks (SR-151/SR-152), never alone.

Rationale

Realizes SN-005 and SN-009 — a floor only CI enforces is one the local tree crosses freely, and a secret caught after the commit is already in history. Trusting the agent to run the checks was rejected: a floor exists for the times the agent forgets, so it is git-enforced and agent-neutral. Parents the interpreter probe: a hook that crashes cryptically because no python3 resolves, or because a Windows Store alias exits nonzero, has not run the floor — so probing by RUNNING a candidate and reporting clearly is machinery serving THIS obligation, and it decomposes to LLR-021 rather than standing as a requirement of its own.

SR-026Coordinator resumes headlessre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered coordinator shall resume headless with stdin closed, never blocking on a prompt: a worker resumes from its explicit claimed assignment plus the committed trailer evidence on its branch, and the integrator derives claim and queue state from trunk history alone — the generated status surface never a session input.

Rationale

Realizes SN-006 and the dissolved edge expectation that an unattended run never blocks on a prompt, at launch or mid-run. The acceptance is deliberately narrower than it once was: it had carried two obligations the shall never stated - transient-limit backoff and stall abort - and an acceptance cell cannot mint a requirement. Both were MINTED rather than deleted, because each describes live behaviour worth keeping: SR-171 and SR-172. An unattended run blocked on a prompt is indistinguishable from a hung one and holds its lane until an operator notices. Keeping a separate serial resume path beside the dispatcher was rejected: two authorities over one decision drift, and the divergence surfaces as a run that resumes differently depending on how it was started.

SR-028Coordinator typed outcomesre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered coordinator shall end each session in a typed outcome code, guard a zero-commit HEAD, and report an all-ERROR stall as an unavailable agent rather than a work stall.

Rationale

Realizes SN-006 and the dissolved edge expectations that a repository with no commits yet (HEAD absent) does not crash the loop and that an all-ERROR run is an unavailable agent rather than a work stall — a coordinator ending in an untyped code forces its caller to parse prose; a session that produced no commit still has a HEAD to report, so without a guard an empty run is indistinguishable from a productive one in the record it leaves; and an all-ERROR run reported as a work stall sends an operator looking for a blocked work item that does not exist. Treating an agent error as a stall was rejected for that reason: an unreachable agent and a blocked item need different responses, so they need different outcomes.

Requirement

The delivered coordinator shall route each in-process session phase (PLAN/BUILD/REVIEW-A/REVIEW-B/DESIGN-CHECK/CRITIQUE) through its declared per-phase command template, falling back to the single declared command — surfacing the declared reviewer dial at run start without enforcing it.

Realizes SN-026 (several model families selected per job, so that work benefiting from an independent second opinion is routed to a different family wherever that is configured) — two samples of one model share blind spots, so a review by the family that built the change agrees with it for the wrong reasons; cross-family routing is what makes the second opinion independent, and one model for every phase was rejected on that basis. Dispatch stays keyed off the in-process session phase because the alternative, a per-phase code branch, makes adding a phase a code change and so discourages adding one. THIS ROW CARRIED A RESUME-SURFACE SIZE TRIPWIRE AND NO LONGER DOES, and the two lenses that reached it are answered here rather than deleted with it. Both were premised on a session INHERITING a resume surface that grows across runs: a view must stay usable as its content volume grows (hat.UX-ENGINEER), and at 3am the reader of that surface is another automated step, which needs the growth legible from the artifact rather than from a human noticing (hat.UNATTENDED-OPS). Neither premise survives the one-engine coordinator — no session inherits a resume surface any more, and the status page is a generated integrator artifact whose size the generator owns, so there is no growing view to keep usable and no 3am artifact whose growth an automated reader must judge. The lenses are not overruled; their subject is gone. If a per-session resume surface is ever reintroduced, both apply again o… [187 more chars — read the registry row]

SR-043Subagent spawn gatere-accept owed

Requirement

While an unattended run is in progress, the delivered subagent-spawn gate shall refuse or defer subagent spawns per the declared subagent-gate dial in the single policy declaration home (off|ask|deny; absent=off; the legacy one-word file is still read through the migration window), honor a launcher-set SUBAGENT_GATE=allow override the model cannot set, and fail open on any error so a broken gate never wedges the tools.

Rationale

Realizes SN-006 (a walk-away run stays safe — bounded, supervised fan-out with the override held by the operator, not the model) and SN-012 (opt-in: absent/off is a vacuous allow, so a non-adopter pays nothing). Supervision, not security — a model that can edit files can remove the hook (adapted from stop-subagent-fanout, MIT; spec docs/archive/INTEGRATION_PLAN.md Phase 4). C-SEC-2 asks that the irreversible actions an unattended run can take be enumerated, each naming the dial or operator authority that permits it — which is this row exactly, for the one action that starts further actors. A direct hit, and the reason this row is not accretion: its parentage was real and lived only in SN-006's `why` cell until the safety half moved into that need's normative text at this same pass. WHY THE FAIL-OPEN ARM IS DELIBERATE: SN-006 asks that the unattended layer keep moving and surface to the operator only where it cannot proceed, so a gate that wedges every tool on its own bug is the failure this clause was written against; what an error never relaxes is the operator-held override itself, which the model cannot set.

Requirement

The launchers at the repository root shall expose every declared runnable capability consistently to an interactive operator, to a direct caller naming one capability, and to automated discovery - from a single declaration, on Windows and POSIX alike.

Rationale

Realizes SN-001 - the evaluator's rungs make running the product never depend on recalling a command, and the capability set is declared once in docs/stack.ini rather than hard-wired and duplicated across the platform launchers. ONE OBLIGATION, not a menu specification: the row states the one capability-level decision - every declared capability is reachable, the same way, from one declaration, by three kinds of caller - because numbering, listing format, declaration grammar, fallback text and exit handling fail independently, which makes an enumeration of them a decomposition wearing a requirement's clothes. SR-049Derived stage from artifact statesre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall derive the stage the project is currently at from the spine artifact states alone, caching it as a derived value — never accepting a hand-set one — with a post-acceptance amendment dropping the derived stage exactly as a newly introduced draft does, and the pending-amendment count carried beside the draft count so the pending state never hides.

Rationale

SSOT applied to the gate itself: a hand-set marker can be bumped without the work; deriving it makes gate advancement mechanical (SN-004) and un-gameable (SN-008). The hybrid cache keeps the value readable on checkout; --check guards rot. SN-029 is a parent because this row's shall is the only place in the SR layer stating that an amended requirement drops the derived stage exactly as a newly introduced one does — SR-139 states which tiers are held, SR-140 what an acceptance record contains, and SR-148 loop selection, none of them the drop clause.

SR-070Generated views are offline, deterministic and drift-checkablere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered generator set shall derive each artifact it produces from the tracked registries alone — self-contained and usable without network access, byte-stable across regeneration from unchanged sources, and carrying a freshness contract that fails when the committed copy has drifted from those sources — omitting a view whose source registries the adopting repository does not carry rather than emitting an empty one.

Rationale

Realizes SN-010 and the dissolved edge expectation that a generated artifact drifting from its source fails its --check, by isolating one independently reviewable obligation formerly carried by SR-038; with SN-012, since a repository that carries no source registry pays nothing for the view that registry would have fed. ONE DECISION PER ROW: the INTEGRITY of a generated artifact and what the state view must SHOW are two unrelated obligations, and this row holds the first alone. They fail independently: a view can be perfectly offline, deterministic and drift-checkable while showing nothing about the work in flight or how the parts connect. The content half sheds along the conjunction SN-023 itself draws ("progress AND how its parts connect") to SR-168 and SR-169; this row keeps the artifact-integrity contract alone. The subject is "each artifact the generator set produces" rather than "each view" deliberately: the knowledge-export bundle is not a view, and a fourth row minted to hold it would be the filler tier the ruling forbids. The child/parent phase spread is untouched and is intended — this split is by observable class, not by phase, a partition that was considered and rejected.

The join, the three coverage edges, the standing constraint and the freshness contract, each driven against a two-component spine small enough to reason about by hand. THE JOIN: assert the design rows are placed where the derived placement puts them, through an interface a design row constrains and through the interfaces its verifying test cases name, and the requirement tier is reached through them, while the files come from their component headers. DERIVED NEVER COPIED: a design row carrying no hat cell still contributes its SR parent's perspectives, and re-ruling that one requirement moves the view with no design cell edited. EDGE 1: a requirement with no design child appears in the unplaced table, is counted there, and appears in no component section - visible rather than dropped. EDGE 2: a requirement reaching two components appears in both and is marked shared in both, while one reaching a single component is not. EDGE 3: seams enter the view, an interface with both endpoints inside a component is internal to it while one crossing two is a boundary of BOTH, an interface is placed by the components its endpoint cells name, and one naming no component is reported as unplaced. NO ACCEPTANCE: with one Accepted and one Drafted component declared in the hand file, no maturity key and neither word appears in any emitted cell. FRESHNESS, DRIVEN BOTH WAYS: the freshness check passes on a fresh view, fails after a registry row moves, and passes again once regenerated; a missing view fails; the written bytes carry no CRLF and two renders agree. THE HEADER: the written view opens with the generated-file header naming it generated and not to be edited by hand, the registries to cite instead and the command that regenerates it. THE TRUNK WIRING: the kit's shipped stack profile declares the view a generated artifact, and the trunk's regeneration step rewrites a stale view so the freshness check passes. VACUITY: a repo whose only CMP row is the inert example row writes nothing and exits zero on both paths.

SR-112Checked per-agent skill fan-outre-accept owed

Requirement

The per-agent skill copies shall be a checked, generated fan-out of the one neutral skill source.

Rationale

Realizes the dissolved edge expectation that a generated artifact drifting from its source fails its --check — one skill maintained in three agent-specific copies rots into three different skills, and the copy an agent actually loads is the one nobody edited. Maintaining a single shared directory was rejected because each agent harness looks in its own path; the fan-out is forced, so the copies are generated and drift is a finding. Generated marking is what stops a maintainer editing a disposable copy.

The skills are part of that playbook, and each agent harness loads them from its own copy; each copy generated from the one neutral skill source, with a copy diverging from it byte for byte detected and refreshed by one command, is that sameness for the skills: every agent loads the text the source holds, and no agent's copy can quietly become a different skill. The generator and its check deliver it with no party between; the need's agent-neutral enforcement clause is other rows'.

SR-139Acceptance as an ordinal over a derived spine stagere-accept owed

Requirement

The kit shall express operator acceptance authority as a cumulative level naming the highest spine tier an operator still accepts, compared against a separately derived SPINE STAGE via a declared, auditable rung ordering — every unreadable or out-of-range input resolving toward MORE operator involvement.

Rationale

The retired three-value enum could not express "TCs are operator-held but LLRs are not", and four tables each re-interpreted the same word with its own fail-safe direction. The failure that matters is a machine accepting something an operator meant to hold, so every degrade has to point the same way — including the ones that look like kindness: clamping an out-of-range level toward 0 reads as "nothing is operator-held" and disarms every hold in the repo. The crossing attribution: B-02 is unarguable - the acceptance level IS the authority input, and every fail-safe clause here describes how that input is read when it is broken. B-05 earns its place on a test, not on the fact that everything here is delivered content: the acceptance clause "Level N holds exactly the tiers the SHIPPED TEMPLATE documents" is a claim about the package's own contents agreeing with its behaviour, which is falsifiable against the package alone with no authority act performed - the same package-wide property class SR-031 occupies. The objection this had to survive is the measured one: B-05 already carries about four fifths of the layer's references, so adding a row to it needs an observable that is genuinely AT the package, not a default. This row has one. That the imbalance itself may be wrong is a separate question about the frame rather than about this row, and it is recorded where such questions belong.

SR-144Every lane close is a terminal state with an immutable recordre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall close a lane that cannot finish into a TERMINAL partial state that merges like any other branch, with one immutable per-close report naming the claimed outcome, the reason, the commit range and the keep/discard split — refusing a report that declares neither a split nor an explicit deferral, refusing a second close of the same event rather than overwriting the first, and refusing a close whose claim is other than one work item.

Rationale

Five successive dedup mechanisms leaked because each reconstructed the return event from a MUTABLE proxy; a document that never moves dissolves the class instead of mitigating it. The refusals are what make "immutable" a property rather than a claim. The split is a field because its absence once merged rejected code onto trunk: silence about it is different from saying "I could not judge", and only silence is unactionable. A claim a dead lane never releases is C-UNA-3's deadlocked-until-morning case, and the immutable per-close record is C-UNA-5's answer to a failure that pages nobody — a close no one can read is externally indistinguishable from a run that finished.

SR-146Prompts are reviewable files with a per-session audit trailre-accept owed

Requirement

Every prompt the delivered loop launches or an attended launcher renders as a review or critique brief shall be a shipped, reviewable file with strictly filled slots — listed by digest in a freshness-gated generated catalogue, each loop session recording which template it used and the fingerprint of what it rendered to.

Rationale

Prose steers the sessions this loop launches and had been reviewable only by reading Python source, which makes the process trusted rather than inspectable. The audit trail is the part that makes the move useful rather than cosmetic: without a per-session digest, "which instruction did this session see" stays an inference. (The argv-vs-shell-string transport decision is design, and lives one tier down in LLR-163.) C-SEC-5 requires that content composed for dispatch to an external model runner carry a DECLARED inclusion rule rather than an implicit one — a prompt assembled inside source is an unreviewed egress path no write-side gate covers, and shipping it as a reviewable file with a digest is what makes that rule readable.

Rationale 37% of the words changed
Two rules decide the shape. A judge's brief must not carry the claim under judgement as its premise - a leaked self-assessment anchors the judgement to it - so every value is registry-, git- or report-derivedreport-derived, and the one claim shown -shown, the lane's report -report, is the template's own labelled subject. And a HALF-filledhalf-filled brief is worse than the generic prompt: hollow sections read as an investigation that was run and found nothing, which is the expensive way to be wrong, so there is no placeholder path at all. The discriminator is a declared cell rather than athe SpecRefreference shapecell's shape, because that inference is unsound - an amendment to a test-case row and an evidence-gap census rowfinding both cite the TCtest-case registry while their briefs give contradictory instructions - and rather than a Titletitle substringsubstring, the fold LLR-161 retired. The amendment brief shows a moved adjudicated link beside the accepted cells because thatan isact naming the `NEEDS-OPERATOR`row foldrecords (LLR-161).it whole from live (LLR-245): a link the brief did not show would enter the record under a verdict that never saw it, and a scoped row left out unnamed lets a verdict and its scope disagree about what was judged.

RoundA review round accepts only a full-lane review with no prior findings or a narrow review that names the prior findings file. render_reviewThe review render strictly fills the shipped reviewer template with the work-item specification, lane range, scratch location, optional review rubric and verdict destination; an empty derived set is a valid round, renders no test command, and states that the row touches no code; listed evidence and reported gaps render beside the test command; render_critiquethe critique render strictly fills the shipped critique template with the work-item specification and named rubric. Both refuse a missing specification, unreadable or empty named input, or unfilled template slot before a brief is written. review_refusalFiling accepts only a verdict bound to the reviewed full commit after the shared review-line reader accepts exactly one line whose keyword, in any case, is VERDICT, in exactly the canonical form `VERDICT:VERDICT: <APPROVE|CHANGES-REQUESTED> findings=<digits>`,findings=<digits>, whose count matches the finding lines the review scorer reads from declared-severity brackets and whose changes request names a finding. round_pathA choosesfiled round takes the lane's next ordinal lane round filename,file file_reviewname, filing writes only a recorded verdict as that round record when the round reader reads its lane path back as that lane's scope, and lane_commitsthe resolveslane's commits are resolved on a branchbranch, and requires theits base required to be an ancestor of the reviewed commit. A first plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when alone, opens with that commit, and refuses a missing rubric, plan or specification, a missing or beyond delta, a coverage failure, or a third round. A second plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when and the first critique's finding identifiers, never their text, uses convergence stance, and refuses a revision that leaves a first-critique finding neither covered nor excluded. A single-plan brief strictly fills the shipped single-plan template with the specification, ordered Done-when clauses, required registry references, and one planner output path; a revision additionally labels the committed plan and latest filed critique findings as claims under judgement. It refuses a missing specification, Done-when, plan or critique, or an unfilled slot. A critique record is filed only when it is bound to an ancestor that holds the plan and has the verdict form; a pass record is written only from committed cited records, passing plan coverage, and a passing delta, after an acceptance or an accepted dismissal of every blocking and major second-round finding. At the cap, a dispute findings file is written only from the committed second critique, giving each blocking and major finding the identifier of its position among all critique findings, its text verbatim, and a declared position; it refuses another identifier set or an existing file. The second plan critique's brief never carries the first critique's verdict or any finding's text. A review round is ordinary by default or convergence: ordinary emits no stance line, while convergence emits one fixed stance line after the range and refuses a narrow scope or unknown stance before writing a brief. An ordinary review reading scope reads the delegated-decisions record and filed plan critiques, while a convergence scope excludes both; a convergence render refuses a reviewer template whose reading-scope command does not carry the review-record exclusion exactly once. The scope critique names the component and interface registries, derived architecture, runtime flows, and dependency ledger, marking an absent registry; the single-plan brief and scope critique render their registry lines from one declared set. A plan critique ties every severity class to a normal-use-reachable defect: a fail-open, data-loss, or security path counts only when a supported workflow or the kit's own routes reach it, and a rare or contrived path is MINOR at most or dismissed. Its confirming round treats a new finding as BLOCKER or MAJOR only when it is a reachable fail-open, data-loss, or Done-when gap; anything else is MINOR. A finding line bearing the convergence-class tag defined by LLR-311 is filed and counted as one finding under the unchanged verdict grammar. The command exits 0 when it writes a brief or files a review, a critique, a dispute findings file or a pass record, and 2 when it refuses, a refusal writing no requested brief or record.

SR-148Autonomous loop work selection: what it derives from, and in what orderre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall select exactly one work item for each assignment an unattended run admits from the repository's tracked registries and git history alone, in this order: ready adjudication rows first, as a stable partition applied at admission rather than by renumbering the ruled rank table; then unresolved handback records; then the earliest incomplete spine tier in SN-to-SR-to-LLR-to-TC order; then implementation work after test-case layout is complete — with the eligible set and its order deterministic, an item whose declared safety, policy or plan-mode inputs are missing, undeclared or contradictory failing closed for that item alone, operator holds applied only from the declared acceptance level, nothing admitted past an operator-held stop, no prose surface and no predefined track in the derivation, no hand-curated next-work or run-phase pointer surface shipped for any live instruction or executable surface to read, write, validate, generate or link, and the status surface a session reads generated and freshness-gated rather than hand-copied.

Rationale

Without one precedence rule, the same repository can resume into implementation while returned obligations or prerequisite requirement tiers remain unresolved. That produces work against stale intent and makes repeated resumes select different next actions. A recorded selection class, source record and hold decision provide replayable evidence of the choice. ONE SR PER (need, property): the loop's work-selection invariant — what the next work derives from, in what order, and that no hand-curated pointer surface participates in it — is stated here and nowhere else, so no second row can drift from it. An explicit three-way partition was rejected: the partition already existed textually and still produced duplicated acceptance. The no-pointer obligation is stated for a migrated repository as well as a fresh scaffold, and the migrated half is the one that matters most: a fresh scaffold never had the files to keep, while an upgraded repository can retain the retired authority files and still pass. Fan-out re-stamp: this row states one decision — what an unattended run's next work derives from and in what order — and its children are the successive stages of that one selection, not separable contracts; the width is the deliberate consolidation of three rows that stated the same invariant into one, so re-splitting to satisfy the bound would restore the duplication the consolidation removed.

TitleRegistry-owned operator gates in shared readiness
DetailAttach to each work row the id and title of every open item its needs cite. The shared readiness predicate, which mutex candidacy also reads, is unmet while a cited item is pending or absent from the open-items registry; such a row reads blocked, with one reason code per holding item naming it pending or unknown, followed by the row's work-item waiting reasons when those edges are unmet too, and its record lists exactly the holding items with their titles. Ruling the holding items releases the row with no edit to it.
RationaleAn operator decision is not an integrated work predecessor; the operator registry already holds its state.

SR-RefsSR-148
TitleDisposition adoption is validated once and recorded at close
DetailA disposition adoption is a fenced TOML block containing exactly one distinct, well-formed successor id. The disposed row is resolved from the title's one event token. For each adoption, validation accepts exactly one strict-UTF-8, parseable specification that is open in draft, queued or active state and whose supersedes value names the disposed row; it refuses every other state, unreadable or unparseable specification, missing title token, malformed fence or request, or unavailable listing. The close validates in the tree that becomes its commit parent and writes the validated ids, in request order, as the closed specification's record in the same rewrite as the close. A replay trusts that record without re-validating successor state or reading history; it joins recorded and drafted successors in one lineage operation, and refuses a request without a record, a record without a request, unequal request and record, a malformed record, or an unreadable merged specification. Every line whose text begins with a fence marker is a fence line; a disposition fence stands at column zero, opens only as TOML and closes only as a bare paired fence.
RationaleValidating at the close fixes the successor relation at the event that records it, while a durable record lets later replay preserve that relation without treating later successor state or unavailable history as authority.

A commit that changes an adoption record or moves a requesting specification into docs/work/completethe completed-work folder or docs/archive/work/completeits archived counterpart is admitted only when it is the close's own commit or carries an existing record with its request unchanged in some parent. A merge is judged only on the changes absent from every parent, under that same rule. The close's own commit has one readable parent, paired moves from one docs/work/activeactive branchclaim folder to docs/work/complete,the completed-work folder, no created or destroyed path outside those moves, the composed close subject, and each changed path outside docs/workthe work-item folders exactly the inbound relink written by those moves as determined by the shared byte-exact relink reading; its record equals its request and every adopted id is valid in the parent tree. The tree under judgement is read strictly; a parent's specification whose front matter or record does not parse holds no record, while a parent git cannot read is refused and named. Every other record change, a carried record whose request changed or was removed, or a requesting move without a record is refused. The rule applies to the lane-commit walk and staged commit check, including their squash handling. Run as the adoption-record step over the commit being made, the rule prints one step line, FAIL with each refusal or ok, and exits 1 when it refuses a record change and 0 otherwise.

SR-150Stakeholder-need cells stay in stakeholder languageacceptance owed

Requirement

The harness shall report each stakeholder-need `need` cell that contains an internal path, an implementation-only identifier or a process citation, naming the row and the offending phrase — at a severity that warns by default and fails only under --strict, exempting a name declared on a reviewed exception list that ships empty (a name that is itself a user-facing interface belongs in a need), and reporting nothing for acceptance or engineering-requirement cells, which SN-033 exempts by its own text.

Rationale

Realizes SN-033 — its accepted acceptance commissions exactly this check, and until this row it did not exist. The need tier was measured clean when this landed (0 of 27 cells), and the row sits deliberately AHEAD of the SR re-tier's churn: locking the clean state in costs one warn-first step now; trusting a large re-statement pass not to dirty it costs an audit later. Warn-first is the ruled posture, not a softness — a form heuristic over accepted stakeholder prose must not gate without an operator ruling, and that ruling has not been made.

Title
The need-form check exits 0 at its default severity and, in its strict mode, 1 on anything it reports
Detail
The need-form check exits 0 at its default severity, whatever it reports. In its strict mode it exits 1 when it reports a finding, an exception-list line its grammar cannot read, or a present registry with no need cell to scan, and 0 when its scan is clean.
Rationale
The requirement fixes the severity, warning by default and failing only in the declared strict mode; the exit code is how the harness and a person's shell read it, so it is stated where the check's output is.

SR-154Independent review routed across familiesre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall obtain, when unattended work reaches integration, each review or critique verdict the declared policy requires from a session that did not author the work — resolved per in-process phase and tier from the delivered agent registry's declared (family x model x tier) rows and only while the declared consent surface that turns managed selection on is present, drawn from a different model family wherever one is configured, degrading only to the documented same-family mode — with every selection logged before launch and a non-converging rework loop escalated through the declared acceptance level, and, where a claimed work item is marked for an in-lane single plan, refuse build output at its making or landing until a pass record binds its plan and Done-when.

Rationale

Realizes SN-026 (cross-family second opinions — every prior carrier of this contract demoted as routing machinery, so the sn_refs join forced the mint; SR-155 cites SN-026 too, for the planner pair, but only this row states the second opinion itself), SN-024 (an author cannot judge its own output) and SN-006. One row because routing, scheduling, scoring and escalation are one delivered contract — that the second opinion happens, independently, or its absence is documented — whose mechanics are the component details below it. The row also carries SN-026's DECLARATION and CONSENT half — `docs/agents.toml`'s pair-rows and the `docs/agents-enabled` surface whose presence turns managed selection on. That half had ZERO textual occurrence anywhere in the SR layer while `orphans=0` still held, because an orphan count proves a need has a citing row and never that the row carries the whole need. Managed selection is opt-in by consent rather than by configuration alone: a repository that declares families without dropping the surface has declared a capability, not turned one on, and the row now says so where a check can read it. fan-out re-stamp: the single plan's independent critique is one obligation carried by its briefs and filing and by its gate; the routing children remain separate.

TitleThe record a merge judges stays as its author committed it
RationaleEvery merge is judged from records - the verdict files, the Done-when checklist - and each of them could be changed by the lane being judged: a reviewer committing work beside its verdict, a later session rewriting an earlier round, a builder rewording its own Done-when. Nothing on a commit reliably names its role, but the coordinator's session log does, so the checks key on it and are re-derived at merge from what was committed rather than trusted from the loop. Reading a round as its session committed it removes the rewrite without adding a refusal. The Done-when claim rule warns rather than refuses because the intake mint still files its derived rows without a Done-when, and a refusal would park every one of them.

Both refuse a missing specification, unreadable or empty named input, or unfilled template slot before a brief is written. review_refusalFiling accepts only a verdict bound to the reviewed full commit after the shared review-line reader accepts exactly one line whose keyword, in any case, is VERDICT, in exactly the canonical form `VERDICT:VERDICT: <APPROVE|CHANGES-REQUESTED> findings=<digits>`,findings=<digits>, whose count matches the finding lines the review scorer reads from declared-severity brackets and whose changes request names a finding. round_pathA choosesfiled round takes the lane's next ordinal lane round filename,file file_reviewname, filing writes only a recorded verdict as that round record when the round reader reads its lane path back as that lane's scope, and lane_commitsthe resolveslane's commits are resolved on a branchbranch, and requires theits base required to be an ancestor of the reviewed commit. A first plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when alone, opens with that commit, and refuses a missing rubric, plan or specification, a missing or beyond delta, a coverage failure, or a third round. A second plan critique is bound to its named lane commit, includes coverage over the Done-when and the first critique's finding identifiers, never their text, uses convergence stance, and refuses a revision that leaves a first-critique finding neither covered nor excluded. A single-plan brief strictly fills the shipped single-plan template with the specification, ordered Done-when clauses, required registry references, and one planner output path; a revision additionally labels the committed plan and latest filed critique findings as claims under judgement. It refuses a missing specification, Done-when, plan or critique, or an unfilled slot. A critique record is filed only when it is bound to an ancestor that holds the plan and has the verdict form; a pass record is written only from committed cited records, passing plan coverage, and a passing delta, after an acceptance or an accepted dismissal of every blocking and major second-round finding. At the cap, a dispute findings file is written only from the committed second critique, giving each blocking and major finding the identifier of its position among all critique findings, its text verbatim, and a declared position; it refuses another identifier set or an existing file. The second plan critique's brief never carries the first critique's verdict or any finding's text. A review round is ordinary by default or convergence: ordinary emits no stance line, while convergence emits one fixed stance line after the range and refuses a narrow scope or unknown stance before writing a brief. An ordinary review reading scope reads the delegated-decisions record and filed plan critiques, while a convergence scope excludes both; a convergence render refuses a reviewer template whose reading-scope command does not carry the review-record exclusion exactly once. The scope critique names the component and interface registries, derived architecture, runtime flows, and dependency ledger, marking an absent registry; the single-plan brief and scope critique render their registry lines from one declared set. A plan critique ties every severity class to a normal-use-reachable defect: a fail-open, data-loss, or security path counts only when a supported workflow or the kit's own routes reach it, and a rare or contrived path is MINOR at most or dismissed. Its confirming round treats a new finding as BLOCKER or MAJOR only when it is a reachable fail-open, data-loss, or Done-when gap; anything else is MINOR. A finding line bearing the convergence-class tag defined by LLR-311 is filed and counted as one finding under the unchanged verdict grammar. The command exits 0 when it writes a brief or files a review, a critique, a dispute findings file or a pass record, and 2 when it refuses, a refusal writing no requested brief or record.

The gate reads only rows claimed by the lane's own active folder at the claim base. The closed planmode set is absent, empty, none, single and dual: absent, empty, none and dual are not gated; single is gated; every other normalized value, and a value that is not a string, is held by name. The closed pre-record change set is the record homes and a close: plan records, review records, decision records, session logs, log fragments, the claimed row's own specification, that specification's move to a closed folder with its report and byte-exact inbound-link redirects, or, as a merge's own changes, the compiled change log and the views the trunk regeneration list names; every other own change is build output. Build output is refused unless a parent holds a pass record binding the row, plan digest and Done-when digest left by the change. A changed pass record is accepted only against its first parent when its nine-key grammar is complete, its delta is none or within and is the plan's own line, its digests match the parent's plan and Done-when, its cited critique is byte-identical in that parent, bound to its reviewed commit and accepted by the verdict grammar, and its dispute pair is both present or both empty; a cited critique record is only round one or round two, and any other round is no record. A second-round non-approval additionally requires an accepted dispute dismissal of every blocking and major finding. At filing and commit creation, the reviewed tree also holds the bound plan bytes and Done-when digest. The gate judges the staged lane change, squash-carried lane commits, and landing lane commits oldest first; a squashed tip that no local branch contains is held by name while the landing tree carries any single or out-of-set claim copy; it compares a merge with every parent and holds unreadable claim copies, diffs, listings, records or parents. Trunk and a lane with no single row are not gated. The Done-when digest a record binds is unmoved by a tick or evidence on a Done-when item, so neither unbinds the record. With the trunk undeclared, a branch whose HEAD holds no claim folder is judged at HEAD; any other branch is refused naming the declaration. Run as the plan-gate step over the commit being made, the gate prints one step line, FAIL with each hold or ok, and exits 1 when a commit is held and 0 otherwise.

TierFull
ExpectedBuild output is held at each gate until a supported pass record binds it, and a changed plan or Done-when unbinds it while a tick does not. Unsupported records hold. Record homes and a valid close pass before a record. A rebase preserves a binding and a merge is judged only for its own changes. Only the lane's claimed copy controls the closed planmode set: absent, empty, none and dual do not hold; single and every other value do. Trunk and a lane without a single-plan row are not held. A non-string mark and an unattributed squash hold by name, and a critique round past the cap is no record. The shipped hook step list refuses unplanned build output by the gate's name. A log fragment, and a refresh merge's compiled log and regenerated views, pass before a record; a regenerated view written outside a merge is build output. A pass form or pass-record commit whose critique reviewed another Done-when digest is refused. A pass record renders and reads through one exact grammar; partial, extra-keyed or field-invalid records are malformed, and its delta is one typed line from none, within or beyond. A critique record outside its own plan home, or past the cap, is no record. With the trunk undeclared, a branch whose HEAD holds no claim folder is judged at HEAD; any other branch is refused naming the declaration.

SR-156Bounded lanes narrowing to one gated landingre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall run exactly one work item per lane on bounded, mutually isolated lanes and narrow every lane back to the integration branch through one serial, fail-closed seam that runs the declared checks on the composed tree — parking a failing candidate and stopping the queue loudly, draining claiming to a clean merged stop under a declared pause, and reconstructing claim and queue state from version-control history alone at any crash boundary, never a half-integrated authoritative state.

Rationale

Realizes SN-027 WHOLE — ready work fans out across bounded parallel lanes and that fan-out narrows to one serialized gated seam before anything lands, in the need's own words — with SN-008 (the seam is fail-closed) and SN-025 (recovery from version-control history alone). ONE DECISION PER ROW: "serial integration is one delivered contract" is sound for the SEAM, but lane execution, claim authority and the trunk-side mint of work-item identity are not the seam, and a row stating the seam alone leaves SN-027's FIRST half — bounded lanes, isolated working trees, a worker ceiling — stated nowhere. This row therefore states the whole lane LIFECYCLE (claim, run isolated, close, land), which is what closes that hole; the trunk-only authority contract sheds to SR-170. The two fail independently: a perfectly serialized landing that lets a lane commit a regenerated artifact satisfies this row and not that one. Terminal close is SR-144's and is not restated here — one SR per (need, property), and both rows sit under SN-027 — so what this row carries of it is only that a terminal branch still lands through the one serial seam.

TitleThe verdict record: what carries a governing verdict, and what binds it to the tree it judged
RationaleThe merge gate asks whether a lane may merge while the loop asks which review phase the lane still owes. A shared identity, evidence join, phase span and count keep both answers on the same tree and policy. Logged round evidence is authoritative because its coordinator session establishes reviewer provenance; the self-verifying trailer is only a cross-check and cannot create an approval. Identity binding answers staleness directly and prevents ordering from promoting a verdict for different work. Separate read-only and reset peels protect both contracts: the reader may traverse identity-preserving commits, while the destructive reset path may remove only the verified refresh at its tip.

For a readable claim whose closed Done-when changed against trunk's pre-merge copy underin active/<branch>,the branch's active directory, intake proceeds through the existing arms: when no verdict line or operator ruling in the merged tree binds the closed text's digest, it mints one brief-bearing done-when adjudication row, titled per row and branch so a re-run dedupes, with Adjudicates naming the closed work item and Context quoting each change; when a covering SUCCESSOR verdict carries Dispositions drafts, it mints the Done-when part's own drafts instead - the whole single-kind verdict or its one ## done-when section - and refuses repeated Dispositions inside that valid section or one supplying no draft. A sitting with no or repeated done-when section, or a DONE-WHEN line under another heading, is invalid, covers nothing, and leaves the uncovered arm to mint the goalposts row. review_logsThe readsreview logs read the resolved final-reviewer mode once per call through reviewer_dials and passespass it to every REVIEWreview log's gating_span,gating span, so all readers apply one mode.

TitleThe record a merge judges stays as its author committed it
RationaleEvery merge is judged from records - the verdict files, the Done-when checklist - and each of them could be changed by the lane being judged: a reviewer committing work beside its verdict, a later session rewriting an earlier round, a builder rewording its own Done-when. Nothing on a commit reliably names its role, but the coordinator's session log does, so the checks key on it and are re-derived at merge from what was committed rather than trusted from the loop. Reading a round as its session committed it removes the rewrite without adding a refusal. The Done-when claim rule warns rather than refuses because the intake mint still files its derived rows without a Done-when, and a refusal would park every one of them.

TitleThe trunk is one declared name
DetailThe integration branch is named by one declaration in the policy home, read by every reader that needs the trunk. A checkout on that branch is the trunk whether it is the primary checkout or a linked worktree. The trunk is never inferred from the branch a checkout is on; an absent, non-text or empty declaration, or one that names no local branch, is refused naming the declaration by every reader that judges or writes against the trunk. With an undeclared trunk, path-triggered step selection reads the change as unknown and runs every opted-in step, the readability report skips each declared measure naming the declaration, and the worker preflight's terminal-row check keeps its guard. A scaffold writes the branch it is on into the declaration only in a policy configuration created in the same scaffold run, never an adopter's existing file; in an unborn repository it writes the branch git will create, and when the destination has no repository or is detached, the template's value stays and the scaffold names the line to set. A lane's integration base is its merge base with the declared trunk, in a single checkout as in a linked worktree.
RationaleA declared name gives every trunk-sensitive route one stable identity; guessing from a checkout lets linked worktrees and single checkouts disagree about the same integration branch.

SR-157Spine and work-registry rules fail the harness verdictacceptance owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall report every declared spine and work-registry rule violation — broken joins, integrity and schema faults, leftover placeholders, requirement-form findings and work-item coherence contradictions — naming the at-fault row and cell, gating the declared failure set at the declared gate while advisory classes never change the exit code.

Rationale

Realizes SN-002 (the chain is mechanically verified, not asserted — this row is the boundary-level home of the verdict SN-002's acceptance asks for), SN-012 (optional registries and opt-outs cost a non-user nothing) and SN-025 (the tracked work-item graph the loop derives its next work from is kept coherent). One row because the adopter-observable contract is one: registry rules produce named findings at a declared severity; which rules, at which severities, is the component detail the rows below it decompose. Fan-out re-stamp: the delivered contract is one — a named, row-and-cell-attributed finding at a declared severity, gating or advisory — while the rule inventory it ranges over is open by this row's own acceptance ("a rule added at one of those sites is in this row's scope by default"), so the child count tracks the number of declared rules rather than the number of decisions this row makes, and would climb back through any bound a split bought.

The declaration this is read against is the rule inventory the delivered checkers themselves publish — the id shapes, the required cells and the closed vocabularies (with the interface and component entries advisory by their own recorded ruling), the strict flag families and their stated exit contracts, the gating form and provenance findings beside the never-gating paraphrase and acceptance advisories, and the work-item coherence rules with their declared opt-out — each recorded at its declaration site, not restated here. A rule added at one of those sites is in this row's scope by default: an unreported one is a finding against this row, not an amendment to it.

Whether a row that passes every rule says something worth relying on is not this row's claim.

Title
An interface whose reach through the rows constraining it and the cases naming it holds no executable test case is reported
Detail
An interface's reach is the design rows and system requirements whose constrains cell names it, the design rows and requirements a test case naming it verifies, and every test case naming it or verifying one of those rows, a constraining design row's cases including those of the design rows below it in the requirement tree, as a constraining requirement's include those of the design rows decomposing it. Each live interface whose reach holds no test case the harness runs, an observation case being one it does not run, is named on one warning line, and those whose reach holds observation cases alone are named on a line of their own. A count line gives the interfaces reached through a constraining design row, through a constraining requirement, through a naming test case alone, by observation alone, and not at all. The process settings' interface-check opt-out silences the report, and with no live interface row it is empty. The report does not change the strict check's exit code.
Rationale
Every interface is pointed at by a requirement stating its behaviour or by a test case observing it, and reaches a test the harness runs that way; reporting the reach before it fails lets the population land first.

The name is reported, naming the case, the interface and the rows, only when it repeats every design row and system requirement the case verifies: a case verifying neither repeats nothing, and a case verifying one row that constrains the interface beside a row or requirement that does not repeats nothing. The report changes the exit code of neither the strict check nor the integrity check.
Rationale
A test case names an interface only where it observes the behaviour at a different interface from the one its rows constrain; per pair, a row that constrains nothing still needs the name for its placement.

Deliberately NOT folded back into SR-070: a state view that regenerates deterministically, offline and drift-checkably while omitting the work in flight satisfies that row completely and this one not at all. Deliberately NOT folded into SR-169 either: a complete progress view can carry no seam graph whatsoever — the state this repository was in before its interface registry existed — so the two are separately observable and separately buildable. `phase` inherits the parent's 1 rather than tracking its children (which span 1 through 4), because a phase records WHEN a piece shipped, and child-later-than-parent is the ordinary case.

SR-170Shared authority surfaces are the serial actor's alonere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall write the shared records it derives - the compiled activity log and the generated project-state artifacts - only from the serial merge step and only against the merged tree, never from a parallel work branch.

Rationale

ONE DECISION PER ROW: a shared serial actor is a shared MECHANISM, not one decision. This row holds the EXCLUSIVE-WRITER contract alone; ordering-and-all-or-nothing is SR-173's and identity allocation SR-174's, each with its own children. Realizes SN-027's serialization guarantee at the surfaces where a parallel writer would actually corrupt something, with SN-010 (the status surface a human reads regenerates at the seam, never on a lane), SN-008 (a first failure stops loudly rather than half-regenerating) and SN-025 (the surface a session reads is generated, never hand-copied). The serial LANDING (SR-156) and the rule that shared authority surfaces regenerate only there are two contracts that fail independently, since a perfectly serialized landing that still lets a lane commit a regenerated artifact satisfies the landing row and not this one. The three surfaces sit in ONE row rather than three because they share one decision, not three: the serial trunk actor is their sole writer. SR-178Text that has moved away from its acceptance record is reportedacceptance owed

Requirement

The kit shall report any recorded artifact whose text has moved away from the copy recording its acceptance - stakeholder needs included - regardless of any Status movement.

Rationale

THE DRIFT half, separable from SR-140 in the direction that matters: a record that exists and rides its acceptance commit, with nothing ever comparing live text against it, satisfies SR-140 completely and leaves every later amendment invisible. That is not a hypothetical - it is precisely the failure the git-history derivation had, and the reason a baseline on disk was owed at all. REGARDLESS OF STATUS MOVEMENT is the load-bearing clause, not a qualifier. The amendment machinery watches the Status flip, and the sanctioned staged-amendment path deliberately does not flip - so a rule keyed off the flip returns nothing on exactly the rows a sitting exists to judge. Reporting against the recorded copy is the only reading that survives that, because the copy is a baseline OUTSIDE the live file and a walk over the live file can never be one. THE STAKEHOLDER-NEED RIDER is in the normative text rather than left to the acceptance because the need tier is the one a sitting most wants to hold and the one the amendment-watching rules were last to reach: each rule walks the tiers it is given, so without the clause the need tier is left off the walk and no rule reaches it. Needs are compared row by row under the same accepted and traced split as every other tier. WHAT COUNTS AS MOVEMENT is one definition with one home, shared with the amend-without-flip guard: the id column and the Status cell are excluded STRUCTURALLY (the id is the join key rather than content, and folding Status in woul… [817 more chars — read the registry row]

SR-205With the assumption gate on, the boundary rung requires accepted, active assumptions that reach their stakeholdersre-accept owed

Requirement

Where the assumption gate is enabled, the delivered harness shall fail the boundary gate for each system requirement not recorded as coincident and not delivered jointly with a sibling that shares one of its needs, that cites no assumption, and for each requirement that cites an assumption which is not accepted, not active, does not reach the stakeholders of its needs, or is a fidelity assumption naming a surrogate that is not accepted.

Rationale

Without a gate the assumption rows are optional documentation: a requirement could cite a draft, a falsified premise or one landing nowhere its stakeholders are, and still pass. At the boundary rung only maturity can be judged, because test results do not exist until the harness has run; evidence is the release rung's question. The gate is opt-in because it asks for a written argument behind every requirement, a cost a small project may rightly decline.

SR-208Held-rung changes are refused before they landre-accept owed

Requirement

Where the declared acceptance level holds a snapshotted registry's rung for an operator, the delivered harness shall refuse, before it lands on trunk, both a lane's acceptance claim that is not a CLARITY re-acceptance bound to the row's judged text and a marked autonomous commit outside a lane that moves a held status or makes a held acceptance claim.

Rationale

The acceptance level names the rungs an operator still accepts, and an automated acceptance of the spine's own rows is already refused. The frame, assumption, surrogate and component registries carry status cells of their own that no automated path was stopped from changing, because the one setting that would stop it defaults to allowing. A policy that declares a rung operator-held without refusing the automated path is a claim, not a control. A lane can carry an acceptance into trunk even when no automated writer made its commit, and an autonomous commit outside a lane can make the same change; protecting only selected writers leaves the held state dependent on who delivered it. Binding the permitted re-acceptance to its judged text prevents a verdict about one text authorizing another, while leaving an unmarked reviewed trunk acceptance to its operator authority.

SR-209Every commit the loop makes carries a checked provenance trailerre-accept owed

Requirement

When a commit is made from a process the unattended loop started, or is merged in a lane the loop owns from the point the loop took that lane over, the delivered commit floor shall refuse it unless it carries a valid provenance trailer naming the loop and its session.

Rationale

A status change on an operator-held rung can be told apart from an operator's only if every loop-made commit says it is one. Without a floor that holds every loop commit to it, a trailer could appear on only some of the loop's commits and a missing one would prove nothing. Where a commit is made, the condition is who made it, not when: a person committing in another checkout while the loop runs is not the loop. Where a lane merges, the floor sees commits, not processes, so it reads whose lane it is from the commits and judges every commit of a loop lane, a person's included: there an unmarked commit the loop made cannot be told from a person's, and a person's commit belongs in the person's own lane. The commits made before the loop took a lane over are exempt, since nothing then could have marked them. Refusing the unmarked commit at the floor makes the mark total, which is what lets a later check treat its absence as meaningful. The floor where a commit is made is local and a determined bypass defeats it, which is why the merge re-checks a loop lane and the history check stands behind both.

AcceptanceCriteriaEvery process the loop starts carries a marker the commit floor reads, so a commit made from a loop-started process is known as the loop's; such a commit with no trailer, or with a malformed one, is refused naming the commit's subject; a commit made by a process the loop did not start needs no trailer and passes where it is made, even while the loop is running; the same validity rule, a trailer that is present and well-formed, applies wherever the commit floor runs. Where the floor judges a lane's commits at its merge, it reads whose lane it is from the commits: a lane is the loop's when its claim, or any commit one of the loop's own writers made in its range, carries the trailer. Every commit of a loop lane is then judged, whoever runs the merge, so a person's commit there must carry the trailer or move to the person's own lane; the commits before the lane's first trailer-carrying loop-writer commit are exempt from this check; a lane that is not the loop's is not judged. An attended re-claim recorded in the lane, a commit that changes nothing against its one parent, names that lane in the re-claim form, and carries no provenance trailer at all, ends the loop's window for the commits after it; a commit that fails any of those conditions is judged like any other; a later loop-writer commit re-opens the window.

SR-215At a checkpoint, an unjudged, expired or triggered observation test is queued once for re-judgingre-accept owed

Requirement

When a work item merges, a release is prepared or a stage gate is checked, the delivered harness shall file one re-judge work item per due observation case: one with no result, one whose result expired, or one whose declared trigger fires after its work-item floor; with no declared trigger, a change to its declared inputs makes it due, subject to that floor. It keeps at most one open item per case, and reports each observation case that cites no written pass criteria as a warning.

Rationale

Judgements cost time and model calls and vary across sessions. Written pass criteria fixed before the first judgement make the pass reviewable. The closed-work floor and the declared trigger are cost limits the operator directed (the PERFORMANCE lens): no change or checkpoint makes an accepted judgement due again within the configured number of closed work items of its latest record, and a declared trigger replaces input changes with the change or checkpoint it names, so a judgement can stand on changes it never judged until a qualifying change or checkpoint meets the floor or its result expires. First judgement and expiry keep missing or old evidence from standing indefinitely.

TitleAt a checkpoint, an unjudged, expired or triggered observation test is queued once for re-judging
SN-RefsSN-024;SN-008;SN-043

Hat-RefsTEST-ENGINEER;PERFORMANCE
AcceptanceCriteriaA case with no result is due at once, and a case whose result expired is due at once; neither waits for the floor. Otherwise a declared trigger (matching changed files, a change to a module tagged with the named component, release preparation, or a stage-gate check) makes a case due only once the configured number of closed work items has passed since its latest record was committed; a case may raise that number but not lower it. With no trigger, a change to its declared inputs makes it due, subject to the same floor; with neither a trigger nor inputs, only absence and expiry make it due. Inputs and policy are read at the checkpoint revision. An open re-judge item suppresses a second, and the decision runs no model. An observation case that cites no written pass criteria is reported as a warning, never a failure, including under strict checking.

The judging itself is the re-judge item's own.

SR-216Each change is measured by the project's declared readability measures, and a worsening is reported with the part it worsensre-accept owed

Requirement

When a change is submitted for acceptance, the delivered harness shall report together every worsening that the project's declared readability and structure measures find in the parts the change touches, naming each measure and part.

Rationale

Code stays readable only if getting worse is visible when it happens; a report after the fact arrives once other work is already built on the worse code. Each measure keeps its own requirement and its own stamped baseline — cognitive complexity against a per-function baseline is one — and this row gathers what they find for the change in front of the reviewer, so no measure's comparison is restated here. A project with no declared measure has nothing to report, and that is itself reported, because the need's promise cannot be met by silence. Reporting rather than refusing keeps the process proportionate: a project opts a measure into gating when it wants that cost.

SR-217A requirement implemented before its test cases were accepted is reportedre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered harness shall report each system requirement accepted after the project's declared starting point whose implementation has landed on trunk while any of its test cases was not yet accepted for it, reading the order from the committed history.

Rationale

Tests written after the code tend to describe what the code does rather than what was required, so the order is the evidence that a passing run means the requirement is met. The stage ladder puts test cases before implementation for a project as a whole, but not requirement by requirement, and the committed history is the one record of order that no cell can restate after the fact. Code declaring which requirement or design row it implements is the one event that marks an implementation landing. A requirement's acceptance is its entry into scope, so judging only requirements accepted after a declared starting point keeps a project that adopts the rule from being judged on history written before it; a project that declares none is judged whole. A test case is evidence for a requirement only once it is accepted while it names that requirement: dated from its own acceptance alone, a test case accepted for something else could be re-pointed at code already written and lend it an order it never had. A test case not yet accepted is the same gap at its widest, since its passing run shows only that the code does what unaccepted text says; the report names it with a warning rather than withholding the result, which a reviewer can still weigh.

A commit that added a ledger entry is an act and dates exactly each row it carried into acceptance and each pair new in its copies, a pair being a test case accepted in a copy while it names the requirement directly or through a design row below the requirement in that same copy's requirement tree (one whose SR-Refs name the requirement, or a child whose parent chain ends at such a row), so a test case accepted earlier and re-pointed at the requirement, or reached through a design row re-pointed at it, is dated at the act that re-accepts it; a row born Accepted counts at its act, and a row's later re-acceptances are not its first. An act made on a side branch is ordered at the first first-parent commit that contains it, as a landing is, and named by its own commit. The record's first commit at its current path is its cut: nothing before it is read, in any earlier spelling of the record, since no reader is kept for a spelling the record has left behind and its history is cut cleanly there rather than translated; each acceptance its copies carry is known only to be at or before the cut while its ledger records an act, and is unread when the cut holds no ledger, an empty one or a malformed one; in this repository the cut is the vocabulary move, which reached trunk at the declared start. A row moved into Accepted from a word outside the status vocabulary is likewise known only to be at or before its act. Such a date settles the order when it falls at or before the landing, and for a requirement's own acceptance at or before the start; otherwise the requirement is reported as unread, never as a pass. A commit that changes the copies with a flip or a new pair and adds no ledger entry, or whose ledger or its parent's is malformed, is a gap: what it carries is unread, never a pass and never dated at a later act, and so is a requirement or test case reading accepted at the tip that no act in the record accepted. The start applies to the requirement's acceptance only, and test-case acceptances are read over the whole record, so a test case accepted after the implementation landed is reported even when both precede the start. Counting a row's occurrences in a commit's diff is not used, because an act accepting one row while withdrawing another nets to zero. A requirement's implementation lands at the earliest first-parent commit adding a back-link line naming it or one of its design rows, read with the one back-link grammar the reverse back-link scan defines. A shallow clone, a start commit that no longer exists or is not a first-parent ancestor of trunk, a start before the TOML registries, and registries still under an older carrier are reported as unreadable, never as a pass, the design registry held to both carrier rules with the requirement and test-case registries, since a test case reaching a requirement through a design row the TOML reader cannot see would otherwise drop out in silence; a rewrite that keeps the start on trunk is read as the history it now is. The harness's checks gain a warn-only built-in step for this order. SR-218The state view shows, for each need, the assumptions it relies on and whether any has been shown falsere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered state view shall show, for each stakeholder need, the assumptions its requirements rely on, with each assumption's status, validity and falsifier and the test cases whose failure shows it false.

Rationale

The need promises that a reviewer can see what each outcome relies on and whether any of it has been shown false. The per-assumption reports and the acceptance brief answer other questions — what is wrong now, and what is being accepted — and neither lets a reviewer start from an outcome. Deriving the view from the registries keeps it from going stale the way a hand-written summary does, and marking a falsified premise in words as well as color keeps the signal readable for a reader who does not see color.

SR-220Overlapping queued work is consolidated through one judgement per queue statere-accept owed

Requirement

While the queued work items include a set that overlaps, the delivered loop content shall hand that set to a single judgement, at most once for any one state of the queued work items and never while another judgement is in progress, queued over an item of the set, or queued to run before it, whose outcome takes effect only as a recorded restructuring in which each absorbed item is closed in a terminal state naming its one successor, its scope text unchanged.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-025 asks that no human curate what comes next; its acceptance states only that the next work derives from the tracked work-item graph, which a stranger reading it would derive as work selection alone. This row states what that promise needs once the loop also mints work: rows minted one finding at a time overlap, and without this row either a human merges them, which is the curation the need rules out, or the loop builds the same job more than once. Two lenses shape it. UNATTENDED-OPS: an overlap is a standing state, so a judgement fired on it re-asks the same question on every idle tick unless the judged state is remembered past the judging row's close, an unbounded retry that pages nobody. PERFORMANCE: each judgement is a strong-tier session, so asking once per queue state is the operating-cost bound rather than an optimisation. The restructuring is recorded rather than done by deletion so that an absorbed item's scope and its successor stay readable after the act. Fed back to the need: SN-025's acceptance could name the loop keeping its own queue free of duplicated work; until it does, this row is derived and says so. Choosing the next work stays SR-148's, and reporting an overlap as a warning stays SR-157's.

SR-222Every model session is recorded in one usage record, whichever provider CLI serves itre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall record every model session it launches, whichever provider command-line runner serves it, in one usage record: token usage under a published usage vocabulary pinned to a named revision, input counted inclusive of cached input, fresh input derived by one formula, the runner's raw usage kept verbatim, the route's provider filled from its roster row for every routed call, the runner named, the vocabulary's gen_ai.provider.name holding the runner's default provider for claude and codex and empty for any other runner, with runner reconfiguration to another provider not detected, and the context occupancy of the session's latest request kept apart from its billed tokens; for a runner other than claude, codex and opencode, the runner name is left empty, and so is every count or raw usage the loop cannot read from the runner's output.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-026 asks that the operator can configure several model families and route work among them per job and capability level; it does not name a usage record, so this obligation arrives through two lenses rather than through the need's text. The performance lens listens for measurements that cannot be compared, or are unavailable, being read as a reliable total: routing among families is a cost and quality choice, and the choice is blind when one family's calls record their usage and another's do not, or when the runners disagree on what "input tokens" means (two count cached input apart from input, one counts it inside), so one column would hold two incompatible numbers. The consistency lens listens for readers disagreeing after a one-sided change: when each launching role keeps its own launch and logging path, a usage fix lands in one path and not the others. A published vocabulary avoids inventing a log format for a problem that is not novel; because it has no tagged release, the record pins the exact revision it follows. The raw usage is kept verbatim so a mapping later found wrong is re-derived rather than lost. Occupancy is kept apart from billed tokens because they answer different questions: billed tokens are summed over every request the session made, while how full a context is depends on the latest request alone, and a session reset that read the first as the second would fire on sessions that are nowhere near full.
