SR-223A guarded session receives the guardrails payload vendored for its modelre-accept owed

Requirement

Where a repository vendors a guardrails payload for a model-name substring, the delivered loop content shall inject that payload, in place of the default guardrails core, into a guarded session whose model name contains that substring.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-026 asks that models be selected per job and capability level; it does not name what a session on a given model is told, so this obligation arrives through the unattended-operations lens rather than through the need's text. A guardrails posture written for one model is ritual noise to a stronger one and too little for a weaker one, and in an unattended run nobody watches a session drift: one core for every guarded model is the silent degrade that lens listens for. Selecting by a substring of the model name reuses the matcher the guardrails policy already applies, so one grammar decides both whether a session is guarded and what it is given, and the repository's own file names carry the mapping. A per-model key in the policy dial was the alternative, and it lost because a model name in shared configuration is the name that rots when models turn over. Fed back to the need: SN-026's acceptance could name a per-model posture; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

SR-224A skill whose description cannot say when to use it fails the skills-index checkre-accept owed

Requirement

The kit shall hold every skill description to the declared description floor: the descriptions it ships are at or above it, and its skills-index check fails, naming the skill, on any description shorter than it.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-005 asks that agents and humans work from the same playbook; it does not name what a skill's description must carry, so this obligation arrives through the first-run-adopter lens rather than through the need's text. An agent reads only a skill's description to decide whether to load it, so a description too short to say when to use the skill is shipped guidance an adopter's agent never reads: the skill works only for someone who already knows it exists, the undocumented-knowledge failure that lens listens for. A length floor is a lexical proxy, not a proof that a description is good: it catches the one-line stub that cannot state a trigger and leaves the wording to review. A reviewer's judgement of every description was the alternative, and it lost as the only guard because nothing would re-ask it when a skill is added. Fed back to the need: SN-005's acceptance could name the skills' descriptions as part of the playbook; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

SR-225A delegated run closes with a record of the calls it made, where the declared dial asks for onere-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop content shall keep the operator's verdict on each delegated decision coupled to the work that acts on it and each delegated run to its record: whatever the declared decision-recording dial, reporting without refusing a record entry that omits a required disclosure field or leaves one blank, treating each run's record as the listing the operator reads, in which an entry with no verdict is not yet seen, and refusing an overrule unless its transition change files or amends open work that cites the entry; and, where that dial asks for a record, refusing to integrate a closing lane whose record is absent, naming where it belongs.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-029 asks that a run released to automation get as far as it honestly can, and that an acceptance it makes on a released tier leave a record naming who made it; it does not name the other calls a delegated run makes on the operator's behalf, the ones too settled to hold the run for and not settled enough to be history, so this obligation arrives through the unattended-operations lens rather than through the need's text. A call nobody is told about is the failure that lens listens for: it pages nobody, and a run that seems to pass does so partly because nothing looked at what it chose. Required fields and a close refusal make that record durable rather than an instruction that can be omitted. The obligation is keyed to a dial because how much of the operator's reading a run may claim is the operator's to set; it ships off, so a repository owes nothing until its owner asks. Every close owes the record, a partial close included, because every delegated run closes with one; a lane the machinery closed with no session present is refused too, and that refusal is a hold for a person to write the record rather than a strand. A malformed entry is reported rather than refused, because the record is there and readable and a refusal would hold finished work for a reporting defect. A decision is an already selected direction, so the operator either confirms it or overrules it; acceptance would falsely imply a new selection. SR-227Where the retention dial is on, adjudication routes retain sessions and reset them only when safere-accept owed

Requirement

Where the declared adjudicator retention dial is above zero, the delivered adjudication content shall manage each retained-class adjudication consistently whether the coordinator or loop starts it: resume the route's active, unheld session in its model runner's resume form; mint and record a session id where the route has no active session; wait a bounded time where its active session is held, then run unretained and state why; record each call like any other; drain the session when its latest request's occupancy reaches the dial or the inputs it judges under change; retire it only when no work it has a stake in is pending, except that at the first keep after a blackout window it retires a session without a last use or last used before that window ended with reason blackout even when its chain is pending; retire it at once when a call fails except that an authentication failure records the failed call and leaves its session record unchanged; let no two calls use one retained session at once; write the retention state only whole, by one writer at a time; make any keep-warm call one bounded turn that never blocks the scheduler; compose both routes' retention request once; and, before retaining a family that uses a dedicated CLI home, read any long-lived credential at each launch from the location a declared environment setting names, keep every verbatim occurrence out of logs, records and commits, and refuse an absent or unreadable credential before launch, naming setup without… [336 more chars — read the registry row]

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-025 asks that a configured agent implement toward the vision with no human curating what comes next; it does not name retaining a session, so this obligation arrives through three lenses rather than through the need's text. The performance lens listens for an operating-cost risk left unassessed: a run that spins a fresh adjudicator for every small work item reloads the spine on each call, and the usage record makes that cost visible, while resuming a session by id uses the provider's prompt cache. The unattended-operations lens listens for a silent degrade: a retained session that has filled, judges under changed rules, or is started in a home whose sign-in cannot be read degrades every later judgement with nothing paging anyone; a coordinator route that bypasses the retained operation repeats that cost and loses the state the loop preserves. One composition keeps both routes under the same drain and lease rules. The integrity lens listens for a durable artifact updated in place without an all-or-nothing guarantee and for a claim nothing can reclaim: two calls resuming one transcript at once corrupt it, so one call at a time holds a session, under a hold that expires when its holder is gone. Refusing an unreadable or absent sign-in before that hold prevents a failed retained launch from changing state or escaping into a person's default home. Retiring only when no work the session has a stake in is pending keeps a review, rework and … [503 more chars — read the registry row]

SR-RefsSR-227;SR-239
TitleCoordinator adjudication shares the keep request and refuses an unsigned account
RationaleA coordinator route that retained independently would duplicate the request composition, state path and account-home policy, so drift in either route could resume a different session or record a different governing input. The shared request is the single join before keep planning. A missing or indeterminate account sign-in cannot safely be treated as a fresh launch: that would bypass the retained home and leave a session record whose authentication context is unknown. Reading the credential at launch rather than retaining it makes each launch reflect the operator's current provision without exposing the value in repository state. Reading an ordinary home without creating it makes refusal leave no new state.

SR-229Coordinator claim admission respects a blackout pauseacceptance owed

Requirement

Where a blackout window is armed, the delivered work-item admission shall refuse a new claim inside that window on every route at any context-guard dial; outside a blackout window, where the declared coordinator context guard is enabled, it admits a coordinator claim only from the current lease holder while that holder's context drain is not latched, the drain latching once the holder's context occupancy reaches the declared threshold and holding across compaction and resume until the operator records a clear or a release, the holder records a hand-back naming its handoff, or a relaunched successor takes the lease.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-027 asks that a declared pause stop claiming and drain what is already in flight, and that recovery never double-assign work; it does not name the coordinating session's own context, so this obligation arrives through two lenses rather than through the need's text. The unattended-operations lens listens for a silent degrade: a coordinator whose context has crossed its declared limit keeps claiming after compaction has degraded the context it needs to close the work it already holds, and nothing pages anyone. The integrity lens listens for a recovery path written only for the unattended run when the same corruption is reachable attended, and for a claim nothing can reclaim once its holder is gone: a retained adjudicator session already drains on occupancy while the attended coordinator does not, and a second or missing holder leaves claim authority ambiguous, so one lease names the coordinator and only the operator's recorded release frees a lease whose holder has gone. A latched single-holder admission boundary was chosen over a one-time event observation because every claim must remain protected when an event is missed or the transcript later reports a lower reading. Fed back to the need: SN-027's acceptance could name the coordinating session's own capacity as a declared reason to stop claiming and drain; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

AcceptanceCriteriaInside an armed blackout window, every claim route, including the unattended dispatcher, refuses a new claim naming the window end at any dial; outside it, with the guard off, admission proceeds without reading or writing guard state; with it on, the holder below the threshold may claim, while a claim with no lease held, a claim from another session or from a caller naming no session, and a claim from a holder at or above the threshold each refuse, naming the recovery action. The unattended dispatcher's own admission remains available without consulting this guard. Occupancy counts the newest valid post-compaction usage on the live branch, including cached input, and unknown usage is not zero. A latched drain survives a lower reading, compaction and resume, and ends only when the operator records a clear or a release, the holder records a hand-back naming its handoff, or a relaunched successor takes the lease. With the guard off, a hand-back reads and writes no guard state. Only the holder may record a hand-back, which names a handoff carrying a session prompt; another or unnamed caller is refused, naming the operator's release, whatever handoff it names; the holder's promptless handoff or own pending relaunch request is refused; a relaunch request left by a previous holder does not block the hand-back; and a subsequent session may take the freed lease.

While a window is armedarmed, hooks act at every dial and deny the closed list of the main session's Agentsubagent-launch call, SendMessagesubagent-message call, Bash/PowerShellBash or PowerShell model-CLI command word, and a Bash/PowerShellBash or PowerShell line unreadable only because of an unclosed single quote, unclosed double quote, unclosed POSIX dollar quote, unclosed POSIX backtick substitution, unclosed dollar-parenthesis substitution, or unclosed PowerShell here-string. One quote-aware shell reading per dialect reads quoted values as the shell does, and treats quoted separators, comments and here-document and here-string bodies as data. It finds the model-CLI command word after leading variable assignments, the timeout and env prefixes, the shell's reserved words, the chain operators and the call operator, and in substitutions written in the line or inside double quotes. It reads a PowerShell assignment to a variable as running its right-hand command, while a quoted or variable right-hand value stays data. A form outside this list gets no dedicated recognition: it may incidentally match this reading, and carries no guarantee either way. window_checkThe guard's window check exits nonzero inside an armed window. At every SessionStartsession start inside a window, hooks inject the blackout close-down instruction; each main session's monitored events inject it at that session's first monitored event in the window and every twentieth thereafter, counted per session per window: bring each open lane to its pause point, using a wrap-up adjudication for an active claim where needed; write the handoff naming each lane and its next obligation; request no relaunch; and end the session. Hook responses inject the latch instruction once and bounded reminders thereafter; inside a blackout window the latch is still recorded, but the blackout close-down, which requests no relaunch, is injected in its place. SR-230Coordinator successor at session exit outside a blackout pausere-accept owed

Requirement

Where the declared coordinator context guard is enabled, when the coordinator lease holder that has requested a relaunch from its handoff ends its session outside an armed blackout window, the delivered coordination support shall start exactly one successor session from that handoff; inside the window it cancels the pending request and leave resumption to the operator.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-027 asks that claiming drain what is already in flight and that a crash at any lifecycle boundary recover without double-assignment; it does not name a coordinating session handing over to its successor, so this obligation arrives through the integrity lens rather than through the need's text. That lens asks what the next reader finds when a holder is gone: a close-out that loses its handoff strands the next coordinator, and one that can launch twice creates competing claim authority. An atomic, owned request consumed once was chosen over treating every session-end event as a relaunch because clear and resume do not end the coordinator and a failed launch must remain recoverable. Fed back to the need: SN-027's acceptance could name an orderly handover of the coordinating role as part of a drain; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

TitleCoordinator successor at session exit outside a blackout pause
SN-RefsSN-027
Boundary-RefsB-09;B-10
Hat-RefsINTEGRITY-RECOVERABILITY
AcceptanceCriteriaWith the guard off, no exit launches anything. Outside an armed blackout window, a request from the holder for an existing handoff launches once at an exit in the declared repository and starts from that handoff. Inside the window, no relaunch is requested or launched, and a pending request at the holder's exit is cancelled and recorded as blackout. Clear, resume, a non-holder, a subagent and a foreign request launch nothing; concurrent exit handling consumes one request once; and a launch that fails for any reason restores the request.

SR-231Coordinator adjudication enters from a claimed lane and accepts only its current verdictre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered coordinator adjudication entry point shall, regardless of the declared adjudicator retention dial, run only from a claimed lane worktree and read success only from a verdict that its own call wrote within that call's deadline. From a claimed lane, it takes only an act an accepted current verdict authorizes. The verdict, reservation, and deadline obligations stated first apply to the judging turn; the act turn's success is the completion contract stated in the acceptance criteria.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-025 asks that a configured agent progress without a human curating what comes next; it does not state the entry boundary for an adjudication the coordinator starts, so this obligation arrives through two lenses. The unattended-operations lens listens for a run whose telemetry lands on trunk instead of the claimed work it judges, leaving a later reader unable to recover its work item context. The integrity lens listens for stale evidence being accepted as this call's success: a verdict left by an earlier or overdue call can make an unsuccessful current call look valid. A lane-local call that owns a fresh verdict reservation was chosen over trusting a caller-supplied path or a shared trunk record, because both leave the evidence's author and time ambiguous. Fed back to the need: SN-025's acceptance could name attributable, current adjudication evidence as part of unattended progress; until it does, this row is derived and says so. An act is authorized only by an accepted, committed verdict, so it cannot substitute later work for the judgement that authorized it.

SR-231 itself — no cell of this row changed
SR-IDSR-231
TitleCoordinator adjudication enters from a claimed lane and accepts only its current verdict
SN-RefsSN-025
Boundary-RefsB-10
Hat-RefsUNATTENDED-OPS;INTEGRITY-RECOVERABILITY
AcceptanceCriteriaAt every retention-dial value, a coordinator adjudication from the primary checkout, an unclaimed worktree or outside a repository refuses before launch; a valid claimed lane exclusively reserves a new verdict path and only one concurrent call can claim it; a successful call returns success only for a valid verdict it wrote before its deadline; and a failed, timed-out, missing or invalid verdict never returns success. From a claimed lane, a later adjudicator turn takes the act a recorded verdict authorizes from the lane head; before launch it refuses an unrecorded verdict, one owing no act, a verdict that judged a row in an unexplained state, or uncommitted lane changes, naming the relevant input. The turn reserves no verdict, writes no binding or outcome, is retained only where the verdict class is retained, and succeeds only when its call succeeds, every authorized act is taken, and verdict records remain unchanged. The reservation and verdict-success conditions stated first apply to the judging turn.

Phase6
Forminterface
CoincidentThe need asks for unattended progress whose evidence a later reader can attribute. An adjudication that runs only from a claimed lane, and that counts as success only a verdict its own call wrote at the path it reserved before its deadline, makes the judgement the lane's and the call's, whatever else the runner wrote or left behind; and an act is taken only as an accepted, committed verdict authorizes it, so later work cannot stand in for that judgement. The row relies on nothing the runner does: it refuses what it cannot attribute. Whether the verdict judged well is the judging session's own premise, not this row's.

ENTRY. coordinator_adjudicateThe coordinator's adjudication entry point runs only from a claimed lane worktree and otherwise refuses before launch through IF-284. It also refuses an unusable route, invalid account, registry error, or unreadable or undecodable brief through that interface; its sign-in reading identifies the adjudicator entry’s account. As its last pre-launch checks it creates the verdict path's missing parent directories and then the path itself, empty and exclusively, and creates its requested-kinds binding beside it exclusively, so an existing or concurrently reserved path or binding, or one whose parent cannot be created, also refuses; its exclusive binding is made through the shared bind_pending request binder; a pre-launch refusal removes only the reservation and binding this call created and leaves any directory it created. Otherwise it composes the shared request, plans the keep, launches and records an ADJUDICATEadjudication call with coordinator attribution, then validates the verdict and records accepted only when that validation and a successful call - exit 0, in deadline, and no reported error result - both hold, otherwise failed, and commits that binding in its own telemetry commit, and prints the IF-285 reading. A non-zero exit, timeout or reported error result returns the failed-call outcome through IF-284 without reading the verdict; after a successful call, an empty reservation is a missing verdict recorded failed. A launched call leaves its verdict file, empty or written, for inspection. The adjudicator act turn runs under the resolved entry’s declared account, the same account as its judging turn, so a retained act continues that session. The default route and every command outcome are declared by IF-283 and IF-284, and the command also exposes a sign-in reading. An act invocation from a claimed clean lane derives a complete later-turn brief from the verdict and binding committed at HEAD, plans retention by that verdict class, and launches and logs the adjudicator call without reserving a verdict or recording an outcome. It refuses before launch for a lane, route, uncommitted lane change, or act-derivation refusal, naming the relevant input; it succeeds only after a successful call leaves no authorized act owed and no changed verdict record, otherwise fails, and a sign-in refusal reports its distinct result. Under the loop marker, each prompt it launches ends with loop provenance after its binding is read. The fresh verdict reservation, validation, and deadline conditions above apply to the judging turn; the act turn instead uses the later completion conditions stated here.

TitleAct assembly from a committed recorded verdict
DetailFrom a recorded verdict and its binding as committed at a revision, the act assembler derives every authorized act that the revision's committed registries and records do not carry in full. A first-acceptance APPROVE act is derived only on a released rung; an amendment CLARITY act is derived on either rung with the verdict named when a listed row is held; an amendment MEANING act is derived only from a bless-marked row on a released rung. RETURN, unmarked or held MEANING, held APPROVE and Done-when verdict parts derive no act. Each authorized row is owed or taken by its committed status and whole-row recorded copy; any unrecognized state or unmatched tier refuses the whole derivation naming the row. An owed first-acceptance flip waits when a parent the parent-first rule reads for it would not claim acceptance after the act, being neither accepted at the revision nor flipped by the act; a flip under a waiting parent therefore waits too. The parent-first rule's own findings decide this, over the registries that rule reads at the revision, and a registry among them that cannot be read or does not parse refuses the whole derivation naming it. A waiting flip stays owed: the brief does not list it for flipping and names it with each parent it waits on and that parent's status, and once each such parent claims acceptance the same verdict's act lists it. SR-232Combined adjudication preserves each requested judgementre-accept owed

Requirement

Where one lane checkpoint requests several declared adjudication kinds, the delivered adjudication content shall present and validate one sitting that preserves each kind's own scope, evidence and decision grammar.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-025 asks for unattended progress but does not require one sitting to carry several judgements. The unattended-operations lens catches a passing checkpoint where a requested kind was never judged; the integrity-recoverability lens catches a partial write where one kind acts while another section refuses. A composed sitting was chosen so each judgement remains independently checkable while sharing its checkpoint. Fed back to the need: SN-025's acceptance could name bounded, attributable checkpoint adjudication; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

Forminterface
CoincidentThe need asks for unattended progress that loses no judgement it asked for. A combined sitting that names exactly the kinds bound at its reservation, gives each its own scoped section in its own grammar, and is refused whole when a section is missing, extra, repeated or invalid, acting on no kind's scope, is that outcome: no checkpoint passes with a requested kind unjudged, and no kind acts beside another's refusal. Whether each section judged well is the judging session's own premise, not this row's.

Detail 7% of the words changed
A combined class accepts only amendment:<id>, first-acceptance:<id> and done-when:<id> Adjudicates tokens; it composes each named class through composethe shared brief composer with that section's verdict path in fixed amendment, first-acceptance, done-when order, and refuses whole if any section cannot compose. One parser reads machine lines one physical line at a time: every line whose first token is a machine keyword counts, complete or not, so a bare, split, bad-label or field-missing line invalidates. The same module'sgrammar's review_linereview-line reader is the one reader of a review VERDICT line: exactly one case-insensitive VERDICT keyword line is accepted only as `VERDICT: <APPROVE|CHANGES-REQUESTED> findings=<digits>`; the filing boundary refuses every other form and the merge reader treats it as no verdict. A combined sitting names exactly the kinds bound at reservation in <verdict>.requested,the requested-kinds binding beside its verdict, has exactly one kind-form lower-case section per bound kind and none other, and has across the whole file exactly one complete line per bound kind and one SITTING line, and no line for another kind; a single-kind verdict has no kind-form section and exactly one complete line for its kind. One binding records pending before either route calls: the coordinator entry point binds the request exclusively at reservation, and the loop binds its composed request at composition; write_bindingthe binding writer is its one writer and record_outcomethe outcome recorder its one route recorder and commit path, returning its `(outcome,outcome why)`with decisionthe reason for it and recording accepted only when call_succeededthe shared call-success derivation has derivedfound exit 0, no timeout and no reported error result, and validation passes. A dispute binding also records the findings file its composed brief names. It is written by the one writer in the same call as the requested ids, on either route. The outcome rewrite carries it unchanged, as it carries the identity cell. A brief that names none binds none, which every reader reads as absent. call_succeededThe call-success derivation is derivedmade once and shared by both routes; a failed call is recorded failed without its verdict being read, and the loop consumes that same whyreason as its completion obligation. The coordinator validates its pending binding before recording its outcome, while the loop records against the kinds read back from its bound request; later consumers use the recorded-verdict reader, which returns only an accepted, bound, valid verdict and each part's row rulings. Every row an adjudication merge act flips needs an ACCEPT ruling in an accepted first-acceptance part, and every row it re-accepts needs a CLARITY ruling, or a MEANING ruling carrying the bless mark, in an accepted amendment part among the branch's own bindings, whether or not the act names a verdict; a recorded verdict over other rows authorizes nothing, and a named verdict must authorize each row its act re-accepts in the same way. Failed, pending, unbound or other-class verdicts cover nothing. Ordinary and mixed lanes consume the same claimed-row reader at the merge: raw scope parsing, the complete acted set including ledger-only acceptances, and the route’s normalized brief cannot give one consumer authority another does not see. Token and section parsing are shared by composition, validation, act scopes and merge-time minting; the class is routed and retainable through BRIEF_PROMPTS.the declared brief-prompt table. An amendment verdict's `- [MEANING+BLESS]` row tag reads MEANING to every rulings reader, and a dedicated reader returns only rows so marked, treating a row without the mark or also tagged plain MEANING or CLARITY as not blessed. One reader of the rows a recorded verdict authorizes, a MEANING row only when so marked, serves both the merge and the act assembler.

RationaleA shared checkpoint reduces adjudication launches only if no constituent judgement loses its scope or grammar. One parser prevents composition, validation and later acts from interpreting the same sitting differently. An adjudication machine line that repeats a declared field reads its last copy; only a model writing the same field twice on one line produces that form, which is outside the bound of lines the kit’s reviewer and adjudicator routes write.

SR-234Contested or repeated review findings receive a bounded adjudicationre-accept owed

Requirement

Where a review finding is contested by the builder or coordinator, or recurs for a third review round, the delivered adjudication content shall preserve each requested finding, the position held on it and its relevant change scope, accept only a verdict that rules every requested finding exactly once as a fix, a successor row, a reasoned dismissal in a declared class, or an escalation to the operator, and direct the dispute sitting to rule out a successor row for a fail-open, data-loss, or Done-when-gap finding.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-006 asks an unattended run to report failures clearly and surface to an operator when it cannot proceed, but it does not state who ends a contested or repeated review finding. The unattended-operations lens listens for an unbounded review loop in which the coordinator sends the same finding back to the builder without a bounded, attributable decision. A complete adjudication was chosen so an independent call can settle each requested finding without silently adding, dropping or defaulting one. Fed back to the need: SN-006's acceptance could state that contested review findings receive a bounded ruling; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

SR-235Attended independent review verdicts are recorded or refusedre-accept owed

Requirement

When an attended launcher submits an independent review verdict for a work item's lane, the delivered review content shall record a verdict bound to the reviewed commit in the review-round record form the delivered verdict reporting reads, or refuse a malformed or unbound verdict without a record.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-024 requires an independent critical eye and assigns the attended reviewer to the operator, but does not require that verdict to survive as review history. The integrity-and-recoverability lens listens for a durable artifact updated without an all-or-nothing guarantee: accepting an unbound or malformed verdict can associate the wrong judgement with a lane, while dropping a recorded verdict leaves the next reader with no record of the independent review. A validated record-or-refusal boundary was chosen over treating submitted text as history because the latter cannot distinguish a verdict for the reviewed commit from unrelated text. Fed back to the need: SN-024's acceptance could name a durable attended-review record; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

SR-237Blackout pauses new model work and resumes it after the windowre-accept owed

Requirement

When a declared blackout window is armed, the delivered coordination and unattended operation shall pause new model work until the window ends, preserving each claimed lane at its committed pause point and starting no model work inside the window except an adjudication needed to bring an active lane to that point, then resume eligible work after the window without retaining a session whose prior use predates that window's end.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-027 requires a declared pause to stop claiming and drain work already in flight without double assignment. The unattended-operations lens identifies a high-usage interval as a pause that must not discard lane state, while the integrity lens identifies a stale retained transcript as an unsafe substitute for a fresh resume. Keeping the active claim and committed evidence was chosen over a second held state because it preserves the recovery model.

AcceptanceCriteriaAt a window boundary the end is exclusive, a wrapping interval belongs to its weekday start, and a changed declaration applies on the next reading. A new ordinary call or claim is refused during the interval; an adjudication for an active claimed work item may run to its pause point; the loop waits and retries after the interval; and the first retained keep after the interval retires a record last used before its end while a use at or after the end remains eligible to resume.

SR-238A deadline or interruption ends the session process treere-accept owed

Requirement

When a declared deadline or coordinator interruption ends a session, the delivered coordinator shall end every process in the session process group on POSIX or session job on Windows.

Rationale

A descendant can outlive the direct session child and keep editing the worktree handed to the next session. Ending only the direct child was rejected because it leaves that concurrent writer outside the coordinator's supervision. The bounded guarantee excludes a descendant that leaves the session process group and a process another service starts outside the session job: neither is ended, and the kill does not report it. A POSIX zombie under a PID 1 that never reaps keeps the group nonempty, so the kill raises after the bound. A descendant that denies the kill access to wait on it also makes the kill raise, rather than letting the coordinator continue without knowing whether it ended. Stopping is the need's cannot-proceed case, not a supervision fault: continuing would hand the worktree to the next session beside a writer that may still be live, and nothing can proceed safely past that. Two windows lie outside the guarantee, each sub-second and on no supported workflow's ordinary path: an interruption while the session is still being launched, before the coordinator supervises it, which can leave a running child; and a process that joins the session job while the kill takes its member list, which is terminated with the job but can still be ending, for milliseconds, when the coordinator continues.

The row checks the ending itself rather than trusting the platform to have done it; a process that leaves the group or job is outside its claim, as the rationale states.

SR-239Where the reviewer retention dial is on, loop review routes retain only their scoped reviewer sessionsre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered loop review content shall, if the reviewer setting is malformed, or names a persisted final reviewer while retention is off, read it as retention off and a fresh final reviewer; otherwise, where the declared reviewer retention dial is above zero, resume a reviewer only across iteration rounds for one lane, claim and review phase, keyed by those values and the iteration stage; read an absent, unreadable, malformed, misfiled or differently keyed retained record as no session and start fresh; never keep a reviewer session warm; retire that iteration session when the lane's full-lane round is drawn; run that round fresh, or, where the declared final-reviewer setting selects persistence, on one retained final reviewer per lane and phase that never resumes an iteration session; treat a change to the template a retained reviewer's brief is built from as a change of its governing inputs; and record session-mode and keep-scope as audit-only columns.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement. The Performance, Unattended Operations and Integrity Recoverability lenses identify the operating cost, unattended judgement degradation, and shared-state corruption risk of repeatedly minting reviewer sessions. Repeated fresh reviewer rounds can exhaust the available plan, while scoped identity prevents one lane or review stage from inheriting another transcript. Coordinator-written review-scope and session-generation records, not reviewer-authored text, establish final-review provenance; session-mode and keep-scope remain audit-only. Fed back to the need: SN-025's acceptance could name bounded operating cost per reviewer judgement as part of what lets a run proceed with no human curating it; until it does, this row is derived and says so.

TitleCoordinator adjudication shares the keep request and refuses an unsigned account

SR-240Commit-floor activation before agent routesre-accept owed

Requirement

Where a checkout's commit floor is inactive, the delivered agent routes shall refuse to start and name the applicable repair that activates the floor.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement through the SECURITY lens: an agent route can create a governed commit, and an inactive commit floor leaves that action without the enforcement SN-005 expects. Start-time refusal was selected over a configurable bypass so the route cannot grant itself the authority the floor is meant to enforce.

SR-241Review briefs render only over a matching verified passed-checks recordre-accept owed

Requirement

When an attended launcher requests a review brief for a lane commit, the delivered review content shall render it only when that commit, or a commit beneath it from which only record changes or no changes separate it, carries a verified record that the declared commit checks and the test set derived from the work item's requirements passed on its tree; otherwise it refuses without a brief and names the cause and the step that makes the record.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-004 and SN-008 require trustworthy gate outcomes, but do not say that a metered independent-review session must be withheld when its requested tree is already known not to meet its declared commit checks. The performance lens listens for operating cost left unassessed: a review over such a tree spends the scarce review session on a failure the process can name before dispatch, while a record-only change must not require the same checks again. Trusting the verified record was chosen over running the checks during rendering because rendering then stays a bounded reader of a prior result rather than a second executor with a potentially different result. The coordinator and unattended review routes decompose this shared boundary separately. Fed back to the needs: their acceptance could state that a review begins only from a verified commit-check result.

A non-code change may render with an empty set and reported gaps. SR-243Coordinator calls record sessions without committing outside claimed workre-accept owed

Requirement

When the coordinator's tooling launches a model session, the delivered coordinator call capability shall record the session in the usage record, record its log without committing to the shared line of development when it starts outside claimed work, refuse an unsafe resumed authoring carrier before launch, judge the call's changes against its starting state, and provide the sole launch route for author, critic and REVIEW-A calls.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement, and labelled so. SN-026 requires attributable routing among model families, and SR-222 requires a usage record for sessions the delivered loop launches, but neither reaches a coordinator-started session or states where its record may be committed. The unattended-operations lens identifies a partial or missing call record that leaves unattended progress unrecoverable, while the integrity-and-recoverability lens identifies telemetry committed to unrelated shared work as evidence with ambiguous provenance. Recording every coordinator session through the same usage record while retaining an out-of-work log without a shared commit was chosen over leaving coordinator sessions unrecorded or treating every checkout as a commit authority. Fed back to the need: its acceptance could state that every coordinator-started model session has attributable usage and a recoverable record without changing unrelated shared work. SR-231's rationale supplies the lane-local provenance lens; its adjudication-only boundary remains unchanged.

A coordinator-started session in such claimed work records one usage record and its log commits with that work. A session started from the shared checkout, a detached checkout, or an unclaimed branch writes its log without a shared commit. A refused record commit is reported and is never success. A resumed authoring turn continues the recorded thread and refuses before launch when its relevant record is missing, damaged, foreign, or when an uncommitted relevant record is no older than it. The edit check distinguishes an edit from another call's standard record commit, reports edits, treats unreadable history as unable to check, and never reports a refused or unable check as success. Published coordinator guidance names the coordinator-call route as the only launch path for author, critic and REVIEW-A calls, its blackout refusal and result meanings, and shared-checkout spooling.

SR-244Transcript-derived usage records include coordinated nested agentsre-accept owed

Requirement

The delivered coordination capability shall record once each transcript-bearing model session that coordination completion ingests for coordinated work, including every session an agent spawns at any nesting depth, with its identity and transcript-derived usage; record no already-recorded message, duplicate no service record, grant its record no gate authority, include no transcript text, refuse an unknown source shape, and direct completion to ingest the current session and a named prior-session tail.

Rationale

A DERIVED requirement through the PERFORMANCE lens: SN-026 makes model-family routing a configurable operating choice, but does not require the cost of coordinated sessions outside the launcher result to be visible. The lens identifies an incomplete cost reading when nested work is omitted or a repeated or resumed read inflates it. Recorded probes establish that a resume appends to its existing transcript, that a Claude result excludes sub-agent usage, and that arbitrary nesting occurs; a sub-agent's final hand-back often has no stop record and is complete once the session's transcripts show the agent finished. The direct-child fan-out re-stamp is intentional: the independently observable reader, identity, contribution, recovery, duplication, shape, source-selection, record, CLI, and completion decisions must not be merged. Fed back to the need: its acceptance could require the operator to see complete, non-duplicated usage for coordinated work across the configured families.

SR-RefsSR-244
TitleTranscript usage is finalized once per message
DetailThe transcript reader accepts usage only from assistant message usage, orders messages by first appearance, and takes each message id's last record. A message is final when a non-null stop reason occurs, a later assistant message follows, or, for a sub-agent's last message, the session's transcripts hold a notice that the agent finished written at or after that message: a task notification naming the agent, or, for an agent its spawner waited on, the spawner's tool result for its call. A session's own transcript is never finished by a notice. Only a transcript's last message may remain open; it is named and is neither counted nor crossed by a cursor. A final message without a stop record is counted at its last record as partial, while reasoning is empty unless every counted message reports it. The usage record sums fresh input, cache read, cache write and output, selects the last non-synthetic counted model, and identifies the cli and provider.

SR-RefsSR-244
TitleUsage ingest reports one defined command outcome per invocation
DetailThe usage-ingest command accepts an optional session identity and root. It emits per-invocation recorded, unchanged, open, skipped, refused, absent or unresolved-parent outcomes, each invocation's line naming its role, agent type and agent id, while a transcript refused for its shape is named by its file and field, in the stdout form IF-306 declares. It exits zero when no refusal, absence or record-commit refusal occurred, one when any occurred, and two when no session was selected.
